assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, universal mechanism: dislocation unbinding yields a two-step melting transition with an intermediate hexatic phase and characteristic KT-type critical behaviour. Original, analytically tractable, and a template for how topological defects control phase transitions in soft and 2D matter. It builds on the topological-defect ideas honoured in the 2016 prize, yet the melting and hexatic step is a distinct contribution.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) are the decisive theory authors of dislocation-mediated melting and the hexatic phase; the credited trio matches this and supports a fair three-way prize. Kosterlitz and Thouless's separate, already-recognised role is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over decades by colloidal, liquid-crystal film, and simulation work, including the long debate over first-order versus continuous transitions in some systems. Interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Real systems show system-dependent melting scenarios (first-order versus two-step), so universality is not complete.
Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological defects may weigh against, and my recollection of how the experimental confirmation is split is not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape and minimal-frustration theory brought spin-glass statistical mechanics to protein folding, explaining the funnel picture and why folding is fast and robust. It is a simple general mechanism that organises a messy multi-scale problem, and it fits the Academy's 2021 and 2024 interest in disordered systems and in physics applied to biology and learning.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes (1987) introduced the spin-glass/random-energy view; Onuchic and Wolynes developed the funnel landscape and its predictive framework. All three are in the credited names, though Bryngelson's later role is smaller and a Wolynes-Onuchic pair could be argued; I propose Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson as the best-supported configuration but the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and consistent with experiments and structure-prediction methods, but whether it counts as physics versus chemistry/biology and how directly it was tested is debated; recognition fits the long-term picture, not urgently timed.
uncertainties: Possible classification as chemistry or biology rather than physics.
Relative weight of Bryngelson versus Onuchic in credit is uncertain.
Modern structure prediction rests largely on data-driven methods rather than landscape theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Very high impact and a genuinely new paradigm (moire engineering), with clean theory-plus-experiment pairing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted the flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. This prediction-plus-experiment structure supports a fair prize, though others (e.g. in Manchester or Columbia groups) contributed to the wider field; I rely on the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide and now an enormous field, though the origin of the superconducting pairing remains unsettled and the field is still evolving, so the discovery is mature but its interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Other contributors to the broader moire field are not in the supplied credit.
Possible premature recognition given the young field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller trapped-ion gate proposal and the broader atomic quantum simulation theory laid the conceptual basis for controlled quantum computation and simulation with atoms and ions. Original, clear and enormously influential, and it ties information ideas to many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: The two credited names are a natural pair, and their decisive roles are widely acknowledged. The wider experimental realisation (e.g. by trapped-ion experimentalists) is not part of this candidate's credit, so the pair is theory-only, which is a coherent but narrower configuration.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in trapped ions, neutral atoms and optical lattices is extensive and independent. Recognition is timely given the 2012 and 2025 quantum-technology prizes, though it may overlap with them thematically.
uncertainties: Thematic overlap with earlier quantum-control and quantum-circuit prizes.
Theory-only credit leaves the experimental pioneers unrecognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and stochastic thermodynamics give exact, general relations (Jarzynski equality, Evans-Searles and Crooks relations) governing work and entropy production far from equilibrium, extending the second law to small systems. A strong fit to my own field: simple, universal and rigorously derived results with application to molecules and colloids.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are shared among Evans (early fluctuation theorem), Jarzynski (equality), Crooks (detailed fluctuation relation) and Seifert (stochastic thermodynamics framework). A prize can include at most three, so omitting Crooks and other contributors such as Searles and Gallavotti-Cohen is a real attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in single-molecule pulling, colloidal and electronic systems, so the core results are well confirmed. The field is still maturing in practice, and the debated question is whether it has yet produced a transformative discovery rather than a unifying framework.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over more than three people and priority disputes exist.
Impact on experiment is substantial but more conceptual than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via the magic-wavelength idea, achieved unprecedented fractional frequency stability and accuracy, redefining time metrology and enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. Clear, original and high impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye led the leading experimental realisation and precision demonstrations. The pair is natural, though other clock groups and optical-comb pioneers (already recognised in 2005) contribute to the full achievement.
assessment.maturity: Independent demonstrations in multiple labs and species and the ongoing work toward a redefinition of the second show high maturity. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2005 optical frequency comb prize.
Other contributors to the clock ecosystem are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The AdS/CFT correspondence is a remarkable conceptual breakthrough linking gravity and gauge theories, with wide use from quantum gravity to strongly coupled matter. Very high theoretical impact, but its empirical status for physics in nature is indirect.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 paper is the decisive origin, with Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten supplying the dictionary. The credited trio is plausible but Gubser and Klebanov are not in the supplied credit, so the allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: There is no direct experimental confirmation of the correspondence in our universe, and its Nobel suitability as a physics discovery remains debated. Strongly supported by internal consistency and applications, but premature in terms of empirical test.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is incomplete and contested.
Committee tradition favours experimentally verified discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Anyonic statistics is a simple, general mechanism: particles in two dimensions need not be bosons or fermions. It was predicted in the 1970s and experimentally established in fractional quantum Hall interferometers and collision experiments in recent years, with connections to topological quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim (1977) identified the possibility of fractional statistics; Heiblum's group provided key interferometry and Feve/Manfra and others made collision experiments. Six credited names exceed three laureates, and Wilczek (not in the list) is historically associated with the term, so credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Experimental evidence has grown quickly and independent groups now see it, but the interpretation of interferometry experiments has been debated and non-Abelian statistics remain unconfirmed, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Experimental interpretation is still debated for some platforms.
Credit allocation among theory and several experimental groups is unsettled.
